text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says government aims at increasing economic growth to six percent a year. Policy is based on two basic principles: attracting more investment to increase development and improving the quality of life of the citizens.
- Culture Minister Farouq Hosni tells parliament the government plans to set up 30 new museums and approve 30 million pounds ($9 million) to renovate antiquities in the southern Sohag province.
- European Union's Middle East envoy says will meet U.S. counterpart Dennis Ross in Washington soon.
- Egypt state to sell shares in two companies through international stock exchanges.
- The United Nations says Egypt has succeeded in reducing the burden on the Iraqi people.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the latest high-level contacts of President Hosni Mubarak are aimed at achieving peace.
- Tourism ministry to set up 500 new projects with a total cost of 26 billion pounds ($8 billion) by 1999.
- Israel has increased its defence budget, says in an official statement that Jewish settlements are legitimate.
- Foreign Minister Moussa says Arab coordination is better now that it was before.
- Egypt to broadcast its television programmes via the internet in May 1997.
- Veteran Egyptian theatre actor, director Karam Mutawei dies after prolonged battle with cancer.
